raw_response:
I farm these 9.2 mu the same way most people here do, wheat first and then maize right after. I do not like making big changes. What feeds the family is steady yield, not chasing something fancy. Last year if the wheat looked weak, adding a bit more fertilizer helped, so this year I will still put enough on, but I cannot spend too much because some people in the house work outside and cash must stay in hand. Water from the well costs money, so I will save irrigation for the important times. For wheat, I will sow in early October, use the seed people around here can buy easily, put base fertilizer before sowing, then topdress once when the crop starts to stand up strong in spring. I will irrigate about three times if the rain is normal. After wheat harvest in June, there is no time to waste, so I will get the maize in right away, with simple field prep and one more round of fertilizer. Maize usually does not need as much water as wheat, so if summer rain is normal I give one or two irrigations only when the field is dry. I do what is safe and familiar: spend enough so the crop does not go hungry, but not so much that I empty my pocket.
